Quick answers: 
- SCC recommendation: default to Processor model (Redwood = Processor, Ainova = Controller) and execute our standard DPA + SCC Module: Controller -> Processor (EU Standard Module, Art 28 compliant). That aligns with most of our healthcare customers and minimizes negotiation. Only recommend Controller-Controller SCCs if the customer insists that both parties have independent control over the same data processing activities (rare).
- DPA redlines: we should pre-populate common concessions (liability caps, subprocessors notice period) and provide a tracked DPA for their legal team to reduce cycles. I can prepare the pre-filled DPA items.
- HIPAA / BAA: we can support HIPAA for Dedicated and Private deployments (we run in customer's VPC or dedicated GPU pools). For Hosted API customers, we evaluate BAAs case-by-case — we have customers with BAAs but it requires additional controls and contractual language. Suggest we state: "HIPAA support available for Dedicated/Private; hosted may be evaluated."
- Sub-processors: Stephanie, please confirm. If possible, supply a short CSV that we can append to the DPA.

I’ll draft the recommended DPA + SCC wording and share a tracked copy for Marcus to send to Ainova.

Thanks,
Karthik
Legal & Privacy, Redwood Inference
